analysis.title: European Leaders: Equity recommendations (CIO Equity Selection List)
key_insights: UBS CIO frames Europe as entering a phase of renewal, driven by accelerating corporate earnings and fiscal, monetary and structural policy support. It recommends a diversified approach across sectors.

The CIO Equity Selection List (benchmark MSCI EMU) has 25 CIO Selected European names across five drivers: Demographics and Consumers, Defence and Infrastructure, Financing structural reforms, Industry 4.0 and Automation, and Decarbonization. The CIO Selected designation is not a rating and sets no price target.
No selections or weights changed in this edition. The text was updated for Ferrari, Galderma, Holcim and RWE, and the front page was revised.

Effective 1 November 2026, CIO no longer rates or ranks equities (no Most Preferred, Bellwether or Least Preferred tiers, no top picks). Portfolio-level analysis through CIO Equity Portfolios replaces them.

Target portfolio weights by theme: Financing structural reforms 35%, Industry 4.0 and Automation 22%, Demographics and Consumers 19%, Defence and Infrastructure 12%, Decarbonization 12%. UBS says the weights are not stock-level recommendations or conviction measures.
Industry 4.0: UBS says the European manufacturing PMI reached 50 for the first time in three years. It sees fiscal stimulus and a shift to smart manufacturing supporting the next industrial cycle.

Defence and infrastructure: UBS cites NATO's goal of 5% of GDP by 2035 (3.5% core defence plus 1.5% defence- and security-related spending, with a NATO review in 2029). It expects significant investment in airfields, ports, railways, pipelines, LNG terminals and the power grid.
Decarbonization: renewables were 47% of Europe's power generation mix in 2024, and the EU targets climate neutrality by 2050. UBS expects the share to rise.

Demographics: nearly 20% of Europeans are over 65 versus 10% globally, and health care spending per capita for over-65s is three times that of working-age people. UBS sees this supporting health care, consumer health and luxury.

Financing reforms: the Draghi report estimates annual investment of about 5% of GDP through 2030 is needed. UBS sees the Savings and Investment Union as the route to channel private savings, which supports the bank selections.

ASML: UBS calls the valuation an attractive entry point because the market is over-discounting cyclical fears. It cites tight memory supply and demand, elevated memory spot prices and conversion of DRAM capacity to AI high bandwidth memory. It advises monitoring consumer macro data because equipment orders can be pushed out or cancelled.

ASM International: UBS expects growth in FY26 to accelerate into FY27 as the 2nm ramp drives atomic layer deposition and epitaxy demand through the gate-all-around transistor transition. It names molybdenum replacing some copper and tungsten layers as a medium-term driver. Key risk is a smaller 2nm node than expected.

Infineon: data center revenue should reach a mid-teens percent of group revenue by FY27, and automotive is about 50% of sales. UBS warns that expectations are elevated, so a beat without a guidance upgrade may not unlock upside.

SAP: UBS sees the dislocation in the shares from AI concerns as an attractive entry point. Only about 40% of clients have upgraded, and end of support for legacy ERP comes at the end of 2027. It expects top-line growth to peak around 2027-28 and flags AI-driven seat reduction and pricing-model shifts as risks.

Siemens Energy: UBS says it trades at a significant discount to US peers. The gas turbine market stays tight into 2030, and grid and aftermarket businesses should make up the majority of EBITA by FY30. Risks include lower data center capex and the wind turnaround stalling.
Rolls-Royce: UBS calls it a turnaround case and targets 2028 EBIT of GBP 3.6-3.9bn and free cash flow of GBP 4.2-4.5bn. It notes a new buyback program and data-center power exposure.

Rheinmetall: UBS says European defence has one of the highest growth profiles in the region and sees double-digit annual earnings growth until the end of the decade. Risks are delayed orders, lower spending, a shift of spending to US firms and unclear financing.

Banks: UBS highlights cheap valuations and capital return. Deutsche Bank targets revenue growth above 5% a year through 2028 with cost growth near 2%, lifting ROTE from about 10% to above 13%. Barclays has a CET1 ratio of 14.3%. Société Générale has a CET1 of 13.2% in 2Q26 and returns 50% of earnings. Standard Chartered trades at 1.4x tangible book with a path to 15% ROTE.

Erste completed the acquisition of a 49% controlling stake in Santander Polska, which UBS sees as a catalyst. Santander has met or beaten targets four years running and targets a return on tangible equity above 20% in 2028, with the Webster and TSB integrations as next catalysts.
Raiffeisen: UBS expects volatility. It sees upside from a gradual wind-down of the Russian business or a Russia-Ukraine peace deal, and management guides 7% loan growth in 2026.
Galderma trades at about 48x 12-month forward P/E versus 21x for European mid-cap pharma peers. UBS cites a 26% earnings CAGR for 2026-29 against 12% for peers and says a higher premium is justified.

Ferrari: 3Q26 results led to another upgrade of full-year revenue guidance across all metrics. Plug-in hybrids were 42% of FY25 shipments and 33% in 3Q26, and the first fully electric model is priced at EUR 550k. UBS says Ferrari is not affected by Chinese competition.
Holcim trades at 18.4x P/E, below its 15-year average. UBS thinks company guidance is too conservative and consensus forecasts are too low after 1H26 results beat full-year guidance.
Alcon: UBS says its 12-month forward P/E is at an unjustified discount to its median of just over 32x since its 2019 listing. Surgical is 57% of sales and Vision Care is 43%.

Lonza was added on a sector preference change: UBS is increasing exposure to European health care, which has lagged. It expects industry growth in the high single digits and a margin recovery in 2026/27.

RWE plans to invest EUR 35bn in 2026-31, targets 12% EPS CAGR and capacity growth from about 38GW to 65GW by 2031, and plans a EUR 1.32 dividend per share for fiscal 2026. Prysmian is rated attractive on NTM EV/EBIT and benefits from grid investment and data centers.

Recent selection changes in the history table: Deutsche Bank was added on 3 Sep 2026. Holcim, Rheinmetall, RWE and SAP were added on 16 Oct 2026. Schneider Electric, STMicroelectronics and Ryanair were removed on 16 Oct 2026. Alcon, Ferrari, and adidas (removed) changed on 17 Aug 2026.

market_movers.rationale: CIO Selected. UBS calls cyclical fears overdone, sees an attractive entry point and cites tight memory supply and AI high bandwidth memory capacity conversion.
CIO Selected, added 16 Oct 2026. UBS sees the AI-concern dislocation as an entry point, with only about 40% of clients upgraded.
CIO Selected for the Siemens de-conglomeration, with an attractive sum-of-the-parts valuation and a discount UBS expects to shrink.

sector_views.rationale: Earnings acceleration supported by fiscal expansion, policy reforms and structural drivers. UBS recommends a diversified approach.
NATO spending target of 5% of GDP by 2035 and aging equipment drive a multi-year investment cycle.
Largest theme weight at 35%, with cheap valuations, capital returns and financing needs for structural reforms.
UBS is increasing exposure to a sector that has lagged, supported by ageing demographics.

earnings_insights: Ferrari reported 3Q26 results (already printed) and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance across all metrics. UBS does not give EPS figures.
Holcim's 1H26 results (already reported) were above its full-year guidance, so UBS thinks guidance is too conservative.
Société Générale reported a CET1 ratio of 13.2% in 2Q26, with management treating capital above 13% as excess.
Rolls-Royce targets 2028 EBIT of GBP 3.6-3.9bn and free cash flow of GBP 4.2-4.5bn (company targets, not estimates).
